## INTERPRETATION & SAFETY NOTICE


This document is traditional Jyotish interpretation produced by a
rule-based engine. It is NOT scientific prediction and NOT a validated
predictor of events.

  • NO DEATH DATE OR YEAR is stated anywhere in this document, for any
    person. No death is predicted, guaranteed or implied. The traditional
    life-safety themes that Jyotish associates with the 2nd, 7th, 8th,
    12th and D12 are presented ONLY as elder-care responsibility,
    family restructuring, separation, bereavement SENSITIVITY,
    inheritance/estate matters and health-safety attention.
  • NO DIAGNOSIS is made. No disease or condition is named as something
    that will occur. Astrology must NOT replace medical care — any
    health question goes to a physician.
  • NO FINANCIAL OUTCOME is guaranteed. No rupee amounts appear. No
    profit, loss, repayment or bankruptcy is predicted. Nothing here is
    financial, legal or medical advice.
  • CONFIDENCE describes the STABILITY OF THE CALCULATION AND ITS
    INTERPRETATION — never the probability that an event occurs.
  • Methods that were NOT computed are marked as such and support no
    statement in this document.

Inline labels used in the year sections:
  [TRADITIONAL] [PRACTICAL PRECAUTION] [LOW CONFIDENCE]
  [MEDIUM CONFIDENCE] [HIGH CONFIDENCE] [TIME-SENSITIVE]

## 1 · BIRTH DATA AND CALCULATION CONVENTIONS


All planetary positions are SIDEREAL. The engine requests TROPICAL values
from Swiss Ephemeris and subtracts the Lahiri ayanamsa exactly once.
Requesting FLG_SIDEREAL and subtracting again would double-shift every
body by roughly -23.6 degrees and silently change signs.

D1 interpretation uses WHOLE-SIGN houses (bhava-chalit): a planet's house
is decided by its sign, not by cusp proximity. Placidus cusps are computed
for KP only.

Aspects are PARASHARI GRAHA DRISHTI: a graha aspects the 3rd, 7th and 10th
SIGNS from its own position, each converted to a house through the lagna.
(An earlier build used whole-sign house distance, which is a different and
incorrect scheme; it is corrected here and regression-tested.)

Dasha balance is a fraction of the LORD'S OWN period, not of the 120-year
cycle. Antardashas run from the mahadasha's own lord.

Aspect convention string emitted by the engine: Parashari graha drishti (3rd, 7th, 10th from the graha's sign)

## 16 · KULA DEVATA / KULA DEVI — EVIDENCE STATUS


KULA DEVATA: NOT YET VERIFIED

No deity is asserted. A Kula Devata is a family tradition transmitted
through lineage and practice; it is NOT a derivable function of planetary
placement, and inferring one from planets would be fabrication presented as
tradition.

EVIDENCE THAT WOULD ESTABLISH IT
  1. A family statement, naming the deity, from a documented family source
     (puja record, temple register, household article, elder testimony
     recorded with its provenance).
  2. Corroboration across at least two independent family lines.
  3. Confirmation that the practice is current rather than historical only.
  
  Only after such evidence is recorded may a specific deity be named. Until
  then this section remains NOT YET VERIFIED.

INDEPENDENT of the deity question: service to elders, care of family-held
land where lawful, and honest dealing with family are recommended on their
own merits. Saturn is the antardasha lord and the 7-karaka Atmakaraka in
2026; elder-care attention follows from that structure, not from a deity.

## 17 · TRADITIONAL REMEDIES


[TRADITIONAL / CULTURAL PRACTICE — no scientific efficacy claimed,
no guaranteed supernatural result, all items optional and free]

A · DAILY PRACTICE
  • A regular morning sit-down of 15-20 minutes.
  • Sleep treated as a fixed commitment.

B · FAMILY AND ELDER CARE
  • Service to elders, particularly within the family.
  • Care of family-held land or ancestral sites where lawful.
  • A written quarterly review of commitments and obligations.

C · PRACTICAL ACTIONS (where the defensible benefit lies)
  • Put every significant agreement in writing, with dates and exit terms.
  • Automate savings; keep irregular income out of the fixed baseline.
  • Accelerate debt repayment when the dasha supports it.
  • Keep medical check-ups scheduled; see a physician for any concern.

## 18 · METHODOLOGY AND LIMITATIONS


WHAT WAS COMPUTED INDEPENDENTLY
  • D1 for 9 bodies plus the ascendant, verified against a reference
    dataset and, for one disputed value, against JPL Horizons.
  • 12 divisional charts (D1, D2, D3, D7, D9, D10, D12, D16, D20, D24,
    D30, D60) of the 16 classical vargas.
  • Vimshottari dasha to pratyantardasha level.
  • Exact Lahiri sidereal ingress and conjunction instants for the slow
    grahas, by bracketed bisection on the real ephemeris.
  • A reproducible convergence risk engine, distribution locked at
    12 RED / 9 ORANGE / 52 YELLOW / 0 GREEN.
  • A birth-time sensitivity harness over seven variants.

WHAT WAS NOT COMPUTED, AND IS THEREFORE NOT CLAIMED
  • D27 (Bhreshta) — NOT IMPLEMENTED. 15 of 16 vargas exist.
  • Tajika beyond Muntha — INCOMPLETE.
  • Nadi — NOT AVAILABLE.
  • KP sub-lords beyond the computed subset — PARTIAL.
  • Ashtakavarga for Mercury, Jupiter and Venus — PARTIAL, so the
    classical grand total is NOT reported.
  • Sunset — unavailable; the installed binding's rise/set behaviour was
    inconsistent and the .se1 ephemeris files are absent.

INTERPRETIVE LIMITS
  • Jyotish is a traditional interpretive system, not a validated predictor.
  • Confidence describes calculation stability, never event probability.
  • House framings differ: this engine reports occupancy from the LAGNA
    while Sade Sati is computed from the MOON. Modern transit literature
    is largely Moon-relative, so the same year can read differently under
    the two conventions. The frame is stated wherever a transit is named.
  • Transit obstruction (vedha) — the doctrine by which another planet's
    transit cancels a benefiting transit — is NOT implemented. A transit
    benefit quoted here is therefore incomplete, not wrong.
  • This engine is LAGNA-relative for house signification. A tradition that
    rejects the twelve-house system entirely (treating sign and house as
    synonymous, and leaning on Navamsa to compensate) would weight D9 far
    more heavily than this report does. Recorded as a divergence.

DATA HANDLING
  • No PAN number, death-registration identifier or street address appears
    in any committed artifact. Locality-level references are PII-redacted
    and source-labelled.
  • No birth date, time or chart was invented for any ancestor or
    descendant lacking one.
  • Historical handwritten charts remain reference-only; uncertain readings
    are marked and never silently corrected.

  ANTARDASHA: Mars — natal house 1, 3, 8 — brings courage, stamina and decisiveness.
      H1: courage, stamina and risk.
      H3: effort and competition.
      H8: transformation and shared resources.
      The difficult expression is impatience and physical overreach. With houses 1-8 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Saturn — natal house 1, 5, 6 — brings structure, patience and delay.
      H1: personal authority, burden, the body and the reputation.
      H5: creative output and speculation tempered by having to do the work.
      H6: labour, debt, service, conflict and daily routine.
      The difficult expression is heaviness and restriction. With houses 1-6 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

2 · DASHA ANALYSIS

  MAHADASHA: Venus — natal house 2, 5, 9 — brings value, comfort and relationship.
      H2: savings and family.
      H5: learning, creativity and value.
      H9: dharma and comfort.
      The difficult expression is pleasure-seeking and inertia. With houses 2-9 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  ANTARDASHA: Jupiter — natal house 2, 4, 7 — brings expansion, protection and beneficence.
      H2: family wellbeing, speech and material provision.
      H4: home, land and comfort improving.
      H7: partnership and contracts supported; the 7th lord strong.
      The difficult expression is inflation and over-promising. With houses 2-7 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Sun — natal house 3, 12 — brings authority and identity.
      H3: effort and initiative.
      H12: expense and letting go of authority.
      The difficult expression is ego and heat. With houses 3-12 involved it appears as with the houses adjacent, the stress and the relief arrive together rather than in sequence.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

2 · DASHA ANALYSIS

  MAHADASHA: Venus — natal house 2, 5, 9 — brings value, comfort and relationship.
      H2: savings and family.
      H5: learning, creativity and value.
      H9: dharma and comfort.
      The difficult expression is pleasure-seeking and inertia. With houses 2-9 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  ANTARDASHA: Saturn — natal house 1, 5, 6 — brings structure, patience and delay.
      H1: personal authority, burden, the body and the reputation.
      H5: creative output and speculation tempered by having to do the work.
      H6: labour, debt, service, conflict and daily routine.
      The difficult expression is heaviness and restriction. With houses 1-6 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Moon — natal house 8, 11 — brings mind, emotion and adaptability.
      H8: shared resources and emotional life.
      H11: gains and network.
      The difficult expression is mood and concealment. With houses 8-11 involved it appears as with the houses adjacent, the stress and the relief arrive together rather than in sequence.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

2 · DASHA ANALYSIS

  MAHADASHA: Sun — natal house 3, 12 — brings authority and identity.
      H3: effort and initiative.
      H12: expense and letting go of authority.
      The difficult expression is ego and heat. With houses 3-12 involved it appears as with the houses adjacent, the stress and the relief arrive together rather than in sequence.

  ANTARDASHA: Ketu — natal house 5 — brings detachment and letting go.
      H5: disinterest in speculation.
      The difficult expression is withdrawal and disinterest. With houses 5 involved it appears as in a single-house period the whole reading concentrates on one area and cannot be redistributed elsewhere.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Jupiter — natal house 2, 4, 7 — brings expansion, protection and beneficence.
      H2: family wellbeing, speech and material provision.
      H4: home, land and comfort improving.
      H7: partnership and contracts supported; the 7th lord strong.
      The difficult expression is inflation and over-promising. With houses 2-7 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

      H11: gains, network and income; appetite that outruns structure.
      The difficult expression is overreach and distortion. With houses 11 involved it appears as in a single-house period the whole reading concentrates on one area and cannot be redistributed elsewhere.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Moon — natal house 8, 11 — brings mind, emotion and adaptability.
      H8: shared resources and emotional life.
      H11: gains and network.
      The difficult expression is mood and concealment. With houses 8-11 involved it appears as with the houses adjacent, the stress and the relief arrive together rather than in sequence.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

2 · DASHA ANALYSIS

  MAHADASHA: Moon — natal house 8, 11 — brings mind, emotion and adaptability.

  ANTARDASHA: Mercury — natal house 1, 3, 10 — brings skill, speech and adaptability.
      H1: self-direction.
      H3: skill, speech and communication.
      H10: career and status.
      The difficult expression is scatteredness and over-assertion. With houses 1-10 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Ketu — natal house 5 — brings detachment and letting go.
      H5: disinterest in speculation.
      The difficult expression is withdrawal and disinterest. With houses 5 involved it appears as in a single-house period the whole reading concentrates on one area and cannot be redistributed elsewhere.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

2 · DASHA ANALYSIS

  MAHADASHA: Moon — natal house 8, 11 — brings mind, emotion and adaptability.
      H8: shared resources and emotional life.
      H11: gains and network.
      The difficult expression is mood and concealment. With houses 8-11 involved it appears as with the houses adjacent, the stress and the relief arrive together rather than in sequence.

  ANTARDASHA: Venus — natal house 2, 5, 9 — brings value, comfort and relationship.
      H2: savings and family.
      H5: learning, creativity and value.
      H9: dharma and comfort.
      The difficult expression is pleasure-seeking and inertia. With houses 2-9 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Jupiter — natal house 2, 4, 7 — brings expansion, protection and beneficence.
      H2: family wellbeing, speech and material provision.
      H4: home, land and comfort improving.
      H7: partnership and contracts supported; the 7th lord strong.
      The difficult expression is inflation and over-promising. With houses 2-7 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

2 · DASHA ANALYSIS

  MAHADASHA: Mars — natal house 1, 3, 8 — brings courage, stamina and decisiveness.
      H1: courage, stamina and risk.
      H3: effort and competition.
      H8: transformation and shared resources.
      The difficult expression is impatience and physical overreach. With houses 1-8 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  ANTARDASHA: Venus — natal house 2, 5, 9 — brings value, comfort and relationship.
      H2: savings and family.
      H5: learning, creativity and value.
      H9: dharma and comfort.
      The difficult expression is pleasure-seeking and inertia. With houses 2-9 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Saturn — natal house 1, 5, 6 — brings structure, patience and delay.
      H1: personal authority, burden, the body and the reputation.
      H5: creative output and speculation tempered by having to do the work.
      H6: labour, debt, service, conflict and daily routine.
      The difficult expression is heaviness and restriction. With houses 1-6 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

2 · DASHA ANALYSIS

  MAHADASHA: Rahu — natal house 11 — brings reach, appetite and unconventional routes.
      H11: gains, network and income; appetite that outruns structure.
      The difficult expression is overreach and distortion. With houses 11 involved it appears as in a single-house period the whole reading concentrates on one area and cannot be redistributed elsewhere.

  ANTARDASHA: Rahu — natal house 11 — brings reach, appetite and unconventional routes.
      H11: gains, network and income; appetite that outruns structure.
      The difficult expression is overreach and distortion. With houses 11 involved it appears as in a single-house period the whole reading concentrates on one area and cannot be redistributed elsewhere.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Jupiter — natal house 2, 4, 7 — brings expansion, protection and beneficence.
      H2: family wellbeing, speech and material provision.
      H4: home, land and comfort improving.
      H7: partnership and contracts supported; the 7th lord strong.
      The difficult expression is inflation and over-promising. With houses 2-7 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

2 · DASHA ANALYSIS

  MAHADASHA: Rahu — natal house 11 — brings reach, appetite and unconventional routes.
      H11: gains, network and income; appetite that outruns structure.
      The difficult expression is overreach and distortion. With houses 11 involved it appears as in a single-house period the whole reading concentrates on one area and cannot be redistributed elsewhere.

  ANTARDASHA: Saturn — natal house 1, 5, 6 — brings structure, patience and delay.
      H1: personal authority, burden, the body and the reputation.
      H5: creative output and speculation tempered by having to do the work.
      H6: labour, debt, service, conflict and daily routine.
      The difficult expression is heaviness and restriction. With houses 1-6 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Jupiter — natal house 2, 4, 7 — brings expansion, protection and beneficence.
      H2: family wellbeing, speech and material provision.
      H4: home, land and comfort improving.
      H7: partnership and contracts supported; the 7th lord strong.
      The difficult expression is inflation and over-promising. With houses 2-7 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

2 · DASHA ANALYSIS

  MAHADASHA: Rahu — natal house 11 — brings reach, appetite and unconventional routes.
      H11: gains, network and income; appetite that outruns structure.
      The difficult expression is overreach and distortion. With houses 11 involved it appears as in a single-house period the whole reading concentrates on one area and cannot be redistributed elsewhere.

  ANTARDASHA: Mercury — natal house 1, 3, 10 — brings skill, speech and adaptability.
      H1: self-direction.
      H3: skill, speech and communication.
      H10: career and status.
      The difficult expression is scatteredness and over-assertion. With houses 1-10 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Mars — natal house 1, 3, 8 — brings courage, stamina and decisiveness.
      H1: courage, stamina and risk.
      H3: effort and competition.
      H8: transformation and shared resources.
      The difficult expression is impatience and physical overreach. With houses 1-8 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

2 · DASHA ANALYSIS

  MAHADASHA: Rahu — natal house 11 — brings reach, appetite and unconventional routes.
      H11: gains, network and income; appetite that outruns structure.
      The difficult expression is overreach and distortion. With houses 11 involved it appears as in a single-house period the whole reading concentrates on one area and cannot be redistributed elsewhere.

  ANTARDASHA: Venus — natal house 2, 5, 9 — brings value, comfort and relationship.
      H2: savings and family.
      H5: learning, creativity and value.
      H9: dharma and comfort.
      The difficult expression is pleasure-seeking and inertia. With houses 2-9 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Saturn — natal house 1, 5, 6 — brings structure, patience and delay.
      H1: personal authority, burden, the body and the reputation.
      H5: creative output and speculation tempered by having to do the work.
      H6: labour, debt, service, conflict and daily routine.
      The difficult expression is heaviness and restriction. With houses 1-6 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

      H8: shared resources and emotional life.
      H11: gains and network.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Moon — natal house 8, 11 — brings mind, emotion and adaptability.
      H8: shared resources and emotional life.
      H11: gains and network.
      The difficult expression is mood and concealment. With houses 8-11 involved it appears as with the houses adjacent, the stress and the relief arrive together rather than in sequence.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

      H2: family wellbeing, speech and material provision.
      H4: home, land and comfort improving.
      H7: partnership and contracts supported; the 7th lord strong.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Mars — natal house 1, 3, 8 — brings courage, stamina and decisiveness.
      H1: courage, stamina and risk.

      H8: transformation and shared resources.

  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

      H2: savings and family.
      H5: learning, creativity and value.
      H9: dharma and comfort.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Ketu — natal house 5 — brings detachment and letting go.
      H5: disinterest in speculation.
      The difficult expression is withdrawal and disinterest. With houses 5 involved it appears as in a single-house period the whole reading concentrates on one area and cannot be redistributed elsewhere.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.

2 · DASHA ANALYSIS

  MAHADASHA: Jupiter — natal house 2, 4, 7 — brings expansion, protection and beneficence.
      H2: family wellbeing, speech and material provision.
      H4: home, land and comfort improving.
      H7: partnership and contracts supported; the 7th lord strong.
      The difficult expression is inflation and over-promising. With houses 2-7 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  ANTARDASHA: Moon — natal house 8, 11 — brings mind, emotion and adaptability.
      H8: shared resources and emotional life.
      H11: gains and network.
      The difficult expression is mood and concealment. With houses 8-11 involved it appears as with the houses adjacent, the stress and the relief arrive together rather than in sequence.

  PRATYANTARDASHA: Mars — natal house 1, 3, 8 — brings courage, stamina and decisiveness.
      H1: courage, stamina and risk.
      H3: effort and competition.
      H8: transformation and shared resources.
      The difficult expression is impatience and physical overreach. With houses 1-8 involved it appears as across three houses the effects interlock, so no single one of them can be managed in isolation.

  The three run together. The Mahadasha sets the field, the Antardasha
  selects which of its significations actually operates, and the
  Pratyantardasha marks the sub-window inside the year. Reading them
  separately misses that they are one configuration.
